It’s pretty much been my constant baseline the entire time, without any real breaks or periods where I’ve felt better.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant periods of feeling excessively happy, elated, or irritable, even if it was just for a few days, over the past three years?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any times like that. My mood has just been consistently flat and low, without any of those highs or periods of feeling overly happy.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant anxiety or worry that something bad is going to happen, or have you been preoccupied with worries about your performance or the future, since being passed over for the promotion?\n\nPatient: I don't really feel a sense of dread or that something terrible is going to happen, but I am constantly quietly worrying about my performance and my future. I lie awake at night for hours overthinking about work and money, and I worry that this lack of motivation is actively sabotaging my goal of ever getting into a supervisory role.\n\nDoctor: Do you often feel guilty or worthless about your current situation, or is it more about feeling stuck and not meeting your expectations?\n\nPatient: It is definitely much more about feeling stuck in a rut and failing to meet my own expectations. I don't really feel an active sense of guilt, but I feel empty and inadequate, like I'm simply not smart or good enough to get ahead. Being passed over for that promotion just confirmed that I'm not the kind of person who moves up in life.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling this way for about three years now, can you tell me if there was a significant change or worsening of your symptoms at any point during this time, or have they remained relatively consistent?\n\nPatient: It has been a pretty constant, heavy baseline ever since I was passed over three years ago. However, it has gradually worn me down over time, leading me to slowly give up on my goals, do the bare minimum at work, and completely pull away from my hobbies and friends recently.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that your feelings of being stuck and not good enough have been consistent over the past three years, but have you experienced any slight improvements or periods where your symptoms seemed less severe, even if it was very brief?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had any periods of relief or improvement at all. This heavy, discouraged feeling has been my constant baseline day in and day out for the last three years since I was passed over for that promotion. It just feels like there has never been a break from it.\n\nDoctor: Has this persistent feeling of being stuck and not good enough significantly impacted your ability to function in daily life, work, or personal relationships for most of the past three years?\n\nPatient: Yes, it has had a major impact on both my work and personal life over the last three years. I went from actively chasing every training and promotion to doing the bare minimum and just going home to lie around. I've also canceled on my friends and neighbors so much that they stopped asking me to help with projects, and this has been my constant baseline ever since I got passed over.\n\nDoctor: You've described a consistent feeling of being stuck and not good enough for three years, but can you tell me if there was a period, even a short one, where your symptoms seemed to worsen or if they've remained at the same level of severity the entire time?\n\nPatient: It has really just felt like a steady, continuous baseline of feeling down and discouraged ever since it started. I haven't had any sudden spikes or periods where my symptoms got significantly worse. It has just remained at this same constant, heavy level the entire time.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any specific changes or events that occurred right before you started feeling this way, and have you experienced any periods of normal mood or functioning since then?\n\nPatient: About three years ago, I was passed over for a supervisor promotion I had carefully prepared for, which went to a younger coworker instead, right around the time company budget cuts increased my workload. Ever since that happened, I haven't had any periods of feeling like my normal, motivated self. This heavy, discouraged feeling has just been my constant baseline without any real breaks.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling this way for about three years, can you tell me if you've had any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt like you were back to your normal self or if this feeling has been completely uninterrupted?\n\nPatient: No, it has been completely uninterrupted without a single day of feeling like my old, motivated self. Ever since I was passed over for that promotion, it has just been a continuous gray cloud over everything. It has truly become my constant baseline for the last three years.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement or remission of your symptoms for at least two months at any point over the past three years?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any breaks or improvements like that at all. Ever since I was passed over for that promotion, this heavy, low feeling has just been my constant baseline. There definitely hasn't been a time where I felt better for two months, or even a couple of weeks.\n\nDoctor: You've been feeling this way for three years without any significant breaks, but can you tell me if you've had any periods where you felt like you were getting slightly closer to your goals or feeling more motivated, even if it didn't last?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any moments where I felt motivated or closer to my goals over these last three years. Ever since I was passed over, all of my planning and even my hobbies have just felt completely stalled. It’s just been this same heavy, stuck feeling as my constant baseline, without any breaks at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if you have experienced any periods of significant depressive symptoms prior to being passed over for the promotion, or if this has been your first experience with such a prolonged low mood?\n\nPatient: Yes, this is definitely my first time experiencing a prolonged low mood like this. Before I was passed over for the promotion three years ago, I was very active, motivated, and didn't have this heavy, gray feeling at all. This continuous, discouraged state only became my baseline after that event happened.\n\nDoctor: You've described a consistent low mood for three years without significant breaks, but can you tell me if you've noticed any subtle variations in your symptoms or functioning over the course of a year, such as slight improvements during vacations or worsening during stressful periods?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed any significant variations or improvements, even when I have time off or take a break. The low mood has just felt pretty much constant and flat the entire time.\n\nDoctor: You've been experiencing this low mood for three years, but can you tell me if there have been any subtle changes or periods where you felt slightly better or worse during different seasons or times of the year?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really noticed any seasonal patterns or changes during different times of the year. This low, discouraged feeling has felt pretty constant and unchanging as my daily baseline for the past three years.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any previous episodes of feeling this low and discouraged before the incident of being passed over for the promotion, or is this the first time you've experienced such a prolonged period of low mood?\n\nPatient: Yes, this is definitely the first time I've ever experienced such a prolonged and heavy low mood. In the past, I had normal ups and downs but was always highly motivated and actively planning my career. This constant, discouraged feeling only became my daily baseline after I was passed over for that promotion three years ago.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any previous episodes of depression or low mood that lasted for more than two weeks but less than two years before this three-year period, or was this the first episode?\n\nPatient: No, I don't recall ever having any similar long-lasting periods of low mood before this started. This is definitely the first major time in my life that I've been stuck like this.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any other episodes of feeling low and discouraged like this before the past three years, or is this the first and only episode you've experienced?\n\nPatient: Yes, this is the first and only time I've ever felt like this. Before I was passed over for that promotion three years ago, I was highly motivated and actively planning my career and future. This heavy, discouraged feeling has only been my baseline since that happened.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this low and discouraged, but can you tell me if you've ever had any shorter periods of low mood that lasted less than two weeks, or has your mood been consistently stable before this three-year period?\n\nPatient: I don't really recall having those shorter periods of low mood before three years ago, so I'm not entirely sure. My focus has mostly been on how much my life and mood changed after I was passed over for that promotion.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if you have had any previous episodes of depression or significant low mood before this current three-year period, and if so, how long they lasted and how they were different from your current experience?\n\nPatient: I can confirm that I have never experienced any previous episodes of depression or significant low mood before this. This is the very first time I have ever felt this way, and it all started after I was passed over for the promotion three years ago.\n\nDoctor: You've had this consistent low mood for three years without significant breaks, but can you tell me if you think you could have had a brief period of normal mood or functioning that you might not have noticed or considered significant at the time?\n\nPatient: Looking back over the last three years, I really can't recall any periods where this heavy mood lifted or where I felt back to my normal self. Before three years ago, I was always highly motivated and focused on my goals, so this heavy feeling is completely new to me.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've experienced this low mood for three years without significant breaks, can you tell me if you believe this is a single, prolonged episode or if you think there might be a pattern of episodes that you haven't recognized as separate?\n\nPatient: It definitely feels like one single, continuous period rather than separate episodes. This heavy, discouraged feeling has been my constant baseline ever since I was passed over for that promotion three years ago. There haven't been any real breaks or times where I felt like my old self again.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand if you think this current state of feeling low and discouraged could be considered a single, long episode or if you might be experiencing recurring episodes of low mood, even if they seem connected?\n\nPatient: It definitely feels like one continuous, long-term state rather than separate episodes that come and go. Ever since I was passed over for that promotion about three years ago, this heavy feeling has just been my constant, unchanging baseline.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that you've had shorter periods of feeling low that you've just gotten used to, or do you truly believe this has been one continuous episode without any variations in severity or breaks?"

The consistent baseline of symptoms without periods of remission suggests a chronic condition, which is consistent with both F32.1 and F33.1. However, the patient's report of this being their first episode of depression and the lack of previous episodes suggests that F32.1 might be more likely, but the chronic nature of the symptoms and the lack of significant breaks also supports F33.1.
